q1_issues.issue: Both time adjuncts put an entity witness in the Time filler slot — (Time sk_results_1 sk_quarter_1) and (Time sk_earn_1 sk_quarter_2) — where Time takes a structured calendar term or a bare deictic/named constant, and 'for the quarter' additionally loses the preposition actually used.
'the quarter' mints a fresh witness sk_quarter_2 instead of resolving the anaphoric definite to the first quarter already introduced in the same sentence.
'based on first-quarter results' is reduced to the bare oblique (On sk_expect_1 sk_results_1), dropping the 'based' predicate, so the parse records only that the expecting is 'on' the results.
The plural 'results' is typed as a single individual witness (Member sk_results_1 result) rather than as a group with GroupOf.

q2_gaps: fiscal-period expressions ('first-quarter results', 'for the quarter'): the structured time terms are Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute only — there is no quarter term, and no rule for a period-denoting NP standing in a Time filler slot

clause-level participial complex prepositions ('based on X', 'according to X', 'due to X'): the reduced-relative rule covers participles post-modifying a noun, and the -ing preposition list (during/pending/notwithstanding) does not reach these
notes: Routing 'said that P' to a sealed non-factive attitude and 'expects to earn' to the non-sealing control-verb pattern (complement reified beside the attitude, no tense of its own, controller's role copied in) both follow the instruction set, as does reusing sk_company_1 for 'it'. (Measure sk_earn_1 earning 90 cent_per_share) uses the licensed dimension-noun scale and lemmatized compound rate unit.
